draft.title: Aggregate supply factors
card: Aggregate supply (AS) is the total output that all firms in an economy are willing and able to produce at each price level. Factors that change firms' costs or capacity shift it.
a rise in the economy's capacity or a fall in input costs. Examples are higher productivity (output per worker or per hour), a larger or better-skilled workforce, and new technology.
a fall in capacity or a rise in input costs. Examples are higher wages, dearer energy or materials, and natural events such as floods or drought that damage farms and factories.
A rise in AS means firms can produce more at each price level. This can allow growth in real GDP and put downward pressure on the price level.
draft.remember: Anything that raises capacity or cuts input costs shifts AS out. Anything that cuts capacity or lifts input costs shifts it in.

a.q: Which change would most likely shift the aggregate supply curve to the right?
opts: A new robot system lets factories make more per hour
A flood cuts the harvest on farms across a region
Fuel prices rise sharply for all transport businesses
Many skilled workers leave the country for jobs overseas
a.why: New technology that lifts output per hour raises productivity and capacity, so AS shifts right. The flood, dearer fuel and loss of skilled workers all cut capacity or raise costs, so they shift AS left.
a.clue: Which change lets firms produce more or at lower cost?

b.q: A drought in Victoria cuts wheat harvests, and flour mills face higher grain prices. What is the likely effect on aggregate supply?
opts: It falls, because capacity drops and input costs rise
It rises, because higher prices encourage more output
It is unchanged, because the drought only affects farms
It falls, because households cut their spending on bread
b.why: The drought lowers farm output and raises the cost of grain for mills, so firms can supply less at each price level and AS falls. Lower household spending would be a change in aggregate demand, not a factor that shifts AS.
b.clue: Ask whether this changes what firms can produce, or what buyers want.

a.best: A new robot system lets factories make more per hour

b.best: It falls, because capacity drops and input costs rise
